svg.aria-label: Flowchart: the QA lifecycle with AI, as a treasure map. Illustrative drawing of the process, no data. The numbers are the order on the map, not the stage numbers in docs/CONCEPT.md.
svg.title: The QA lifecycle, as a treasure map

g.aria-label: the map itself is the project layer: context, knowledge and decisions that differ for every project
g.data-n: the map itself is the project layer: context, knowledge and decisions that differ for every project

g.aria-label: the trail: the path one change takes. Everything on it is a draft until a person marks the X
g.data-n: the trail: the path one change takes. Everything on it is a draft until a person marks the X

g.aria-label: 1 requirements: AI reads the story and lists gaps and questions. Output is a draft
g.data-n: 1 requirements: AI reads the story and lists gaps and questions. Output is a draft

g.aria-label: 2 test design: AI drafts cases from the approved brief. A person reviews every case
g.data-n: 2 test design: AI drafts cases from the approved brief. A person reviews every case

g.aria-label: 3 manual testing: a person runs the cases, decides pass or fail and confirms each bug
g.data-n: 3 manual testing: a person runs the cases, decides pass or fail and confirms each bug

g.aria-label: 4 automation, optional: only for a case a person already confirmed. No automation project is in this repository yet
g.data-n: 4 automation, optional: only for a case a person already confirmed. No automation project is in this repository yet

g.aria-label: 5 CI: runs the same way every time. No AI and no skill here, so no draft to review
g.data-n: 5 CI: runs the same way every time. No AI and no skill here, so no draft to review

g.aria-label: 6 analysis and release: AI reads CI failures and drafts the report and risk summary. The release decision is yours
g.data-n: 6 analysis and release: AI reads CI failures and drafts the report and risk summary. The release decision is yours

g.aria-label: 7 feedback: every miss becomes an entry, then a change proposal. A person approves any change to rules, skills or hooks
g.data-n: 7 feedback: every miss becomes an entry, then a change proposal. A person approves any change to rules, skills or hooks

g.aria-label: production: a skull rock off the route. No access, and nothing on this map goes there
g.data-n: production: a skull rock off the route. No access, and nothing on this map goes there

g.aria-label: the compass: rules, policy and permissions. It sits in the middle because every leg is steered by it
g.data-n: the compass: rules, policy and permissions. It sits in the middle because every leg is steered by it

g.aria-label: the ruler: evals. They measure whether a skill or a hook works; the validator checks the file structure on every pull request
g.data-n: the ruler: evals. They measure whether a skill or a hook works; the validator checks the file structure on every pull request

g.aria-label: red X: answers the questions, approves the brief
g.data-n: red X: answers the questions, approves the brief

g.aria-label: red X: reviews every case, saves it to the test management system
g.data-n: red X: reviews every case, saves it to the test management system

g.aria-label: red X: decides pass or fail, confirms each bug
g.data-n: red X: decides pass or fail, confirms each bug

g.aria-label: red X: approves the candidate, reviews the pull request
g.data-n: red X: approves the candidate, reviews the pull request

g.aria-label: red X: decides: defect, test or environment?
g.data-n: red X: decides: defect, test or environment?

g.aria-label: red X: makes the release decision
g.data-n: red X: makes the release decision

g.aria-label: red X: QA Lead approves any change to a rule, skill, hook or eval
g.data-n: red X: QA Lead approves any change to a rule, skill, hook or eval

g.aria-label: test design
g.data-n: test design

g.aria-label: manual testing
g.data-n: manual testing

g.aria-label: automation (optional)
g.data-n: automation (optional)

g.aria-label: CI, no AI
g.data-n: CI, no AI

g.aria-label: the pirate is the reviewer. He walks the trail and waits at every red X until a person has decided
g.data-n: the pirate is the reviewer. He walks the trail and waits at every red X until a person has decided

g.text: 1 requirements: AI lists the gaps and questions.
A person answers them and approves the brief.
2 test design: AI drafts the cases from the brief.
A person reviews every case and saves it to the TMS.
3 manual testing: a person runs the cases,
decides pass or fail and confirms each bug.
4 automation, optional: only for a case already confirmed.
A person approves it and reviews the pull request.
5 CI: runs the same way every time, no AI.
A person decides: defect, test or environment?
6 analysis and release: AI reads the CI failures and
drafts the report. A person makes the release decision.
7 feedback: every miss becomes an entry, then a proposal.
QA Lead approves any change to a rule, skill, hook or eval.
